summary: Iter18 SAWALI — Public legal policies (privacy/services/deletion) tested end-to-end. BACKEND: 15/15 new pytest tests GREEN in /app/backend/tests/test_sawali_iter18.py (~3.8s). Combined regression iter12+13+14+15+16+17+18 = 123/123 GREEN in ~24.2s (pytest_iter18_full.xml). Coverage split into 4 classes: (A) TestPolicyList — GET /api/admin/policies 401 unauth, 401/403 with bogus token, 200 admin returns {items:[3]} with correct slot/label/public_url shape (URL ends with /api/public/policies/<slot> and is fully-qualified preview URL); seed data confirms present=true with filename/size/uploaded_at populated. (B) TestPolicyUpload — POST 400 'Slot invalide' on bad slot, 400 'Format invalide : PDF requis' on text/plain non-PDF, 400 'Fichier vide' on empty bytes, 413 on >15MB upload, 200 happy path returns {ok:true, slot, label, filename, size, uploaded_at, uploaded_by_label, uploaded_from_ip, present:true, public_url} AND persists file at /app/backend/uploads/policies/{slot}.pdf (bytes match) AND upserts doc into db.policies; re-upload replaces atomically (no leftover .tmp file, new bytes match); accept content_type=application/octet-stream when filename ends in .pdf. (C) TestPolicyDelete — 400 bad slot; happy path removes file from disk + doc from db.policies; subsequent GET shows present=false, filename=null. (D) TestPublicPolicy — NO auth required: 404 'Politique introuvable' on bad slot, 404 'Politique non publiée' when missing; happy path 200 with content-type application/pdf, Content-Disposition includes 'inline' + the original filename, body bytes EXACTLY match the uploaded PDF. FRONTEND (Playwright with admin JWT injected): /admin/policies renders admin-policies-page with all 18 testids (3 cards × {upload,copy,open,file-input,delete} + card itself). policy-copy-privacy click → navigator.clipboard receives 'https://sawali-portal.preview.emergentagent.com/api/public/policies/privacy' AND toast 'Lien copié' appears ✓. Sidebar admin link 'Politiques publiques' (data-testid=sidebar-link--admin-policies) navigates to /admin/policies ✓. set_input_files on policy-file-input-services with a fake 410-byte PDF → POST /admin/policies/services/upload sent, toast 'Politique remplacée' appears, card flips to 'Publiée' badge ✓. Marketing footer (visit /) has data-testid=footer-policy-links group containing footer-policy-{privacy,services,deletion}, each with target=_blank and href=/api/public/policies/<slot> (relative — resolves to same origin). Direct unauthenticated requests.get on /api/public/policies/privacy returned 200 application/pdf with Content-Disposition='inline; filename="privacy.pdf"' and 1,510,324 bytes (full seed PDF). Seed file services.pdf was overwritten during UI upload test then RESTORED from /tmp/services.pdf with original 980,056 bytes + DB metadata reset. Screenshot saved at .screenshots/iter18_policies_admin.png.

issues: Footer policy links use RELATIVE href '/api/public/policies/<slot>' rather than the absolute public_url returned by the backend list endpoint. Functionally identical when served from the same origin (Google/Facebook scrapers will resolve correctly), but slightly inconsistent with the AdminPolicies card which uses the absolute public_url. LOW priority — could pull from a public config endpoint or use absolute URL for consistency, but not blocking.

action_items: (NONE — all tests pass) Optional/LOW: consider whether MarketingFooter footer-policy-* hrefs should use the absolute preview URL for parity with AdminPolicies cards.

(LOW, carry-over iter17) server.py is ~7249 lines — splitting into routers (auth/admin/portal/forms/whatsapp/scheduler/automations/templates/timeline/crm_notes_tasks/policies/db) is increasingly overdue.

(LOW) public_policy returns Cache-Control: 'public, max-age=3600' but the response middleware is overriding to no-store per agent context note. Harmless for the use case (Google/Facebook still fetch the file), but if caching is desired the middleware should whitelist /api/public/policies/* to skip the no-store override.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py admin_upload_policy (~2065-2110) writes to .pdf.tmp then atomically renames via tmp.replace(target). Correct pattern: a partial/aborted upload won't leave a corrupt main file. Verified by re-upload test: no leftover .tmp file, new bytes exactly match.

server.py admin_upload_policy size check happens DURING streaming (per-chunk increment + early raise + tmp.unlink). Good — protects from large uploads filling disk before rejection. 413 returned correctly at 16MB > 15MB POLICY_MAX_SIZE.

server.py admin_upload_policy validates PDF via either content_type='application/pdf' OR filename.suffix=='.pdf' — covers the common case of browsers sending application/octet-stream or empty content_type but a .pdf filename. Verified.

server.py _policy_public_url uses x-forwarded-host header preferentially → resolves correctly to the preview URL behind the K8s ingress. Verified: returned URL was 'https://sawali-portal.preview.emergentagent.com/api/public/policies/privacy'.
server.py public_policy returns FileResponse with explicit media_type, filename, and Content-Disposition='inline' header. X-Robots-Tag='all' allows Google/Facebook to fetch + cache. ✓
server.py admin_delete_policy is idempotent on missing files (uses unlink + delete_one which return silently on no-match). ✓

AdminPolicies.jsx PolicyCard onFile() does client-side PDF + size validation before POST, mirroring the server checks. Toast errors match server messages ('Format invalide : PDF requis', 'Fichier trop volumineux'). Good defense-in-depth.
AdminPolicies.jsx copyLink() falls back to a 'Impossible de copier' toast on clipboard failure — handles both Permissions API denial and navigator.clipboard absence in older browsers. ✓

MarketingFooter.jsx footer-policy-* links use RELATIVE '/api/public/policies/<slot>' instead of an absolute URL. Works correctly because they're served from the same origin. Cosmetic inconsistency vs AdminPolicies which uses public_url returned by backend.
PortalLayout.jsx adds 'Politiques publiques' (Shield icon) to admin sidebar at line 42. data-testid=sidebar-link--admin-policies properly generated by the existing slug logic. ✓
POLICY_MAX_SIZE=15MB hardcoded — could move to env (POLICY_MAX_SIZE_MB) for tuning without redeploy. LOW.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all 18 admin testids visible; copy+toast+clipboard mock ✓; sidebar link ✓; upload via set_input_files → toast + Publiée badge ✓; footer 3 links + group ✓; public PDF unauth fetch returns correct bytes/headers ✓)

Tests freely upload/delete during the run. Final state on disk: privacy.pdf 1.5MB, services.pdf 980KB, deletion.pdf 549KB — matches the agent context note's expected seed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter18 suite = /app/backend/tests/test_sawali_iter18.py (15 tests, ~3.8s). Patterns reused: requests.post(files={'file':(name, bytes, content_type)}) for multipart; module-scoped autouse fixture for backup/restore of disk + DB; MIN_PDF constant (~400 bytes valid PDF skeleton). The 3 seed PDFs at /app/backend/uploads/policies/{privacy,services,deletion}.pdf (1.5MB/980KB/549KB) MUST stay intact — backups also live at /tmp/{privacy,services,deletion}.pdf. db.policies has 3 docs keyed by 'slot'. Clipboard must be mocked via add_init_script BEFORE page.goto (re-defines navigator.clipboard.writeText synchronously, captures into window.__copied).
rca of the issue: No bugs found. The Public Policies feature (3 fixed slots, atomic-replace upload, 15MB limit, public unauthenticated PDF serve with inline disposition, admin CRUD with full validation, db.policies persistence, dynamic public_url from x-forwarded-host, 3-card admin UI with copy-to-clipboard + replace + delete, marketing footer integration, sidebar shortcut) all match the spec exactly. Code is well-isolated (~140 lines of new server.py + 1 new admin page + minimal MarketingFooter/PortalLayout edits). Atomic upload pattern (.tmp → rename) and streamed-size enforcement are production-quality. Only suggestions are cosmetic/architectural (relative vs absolute footer hrefs; POLICY_MAX_SIZE env var; server.py is now 7249 lines and overdue for router split).
